general_information.Description: This course introduces students to a number of research methods useful for academic and professional investigations of business practices. By examining the applications, strengths, and weaknesses of methodologies drawn from both the qualitative and quantitative traditions, this course permits an understanding of the various steps involved in designing and executing a research project so that students will be able to conduct their research later. A key feature of this course is the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) tools and applications. Students learn to use theses tools to : - support generating and refining research topics, - assist in content suggestions, - assist in answering questions on Edunext, in-class discussions, and identifying credible sources. - supports summarizing and concluding research findings through data-driven insights and structured templates.
general_information.StudentTasks: Students need to - Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities - Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose - Read the textbook in advance - Access the course website (http://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and materials of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students, and for practicing and assessment.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Write a literature review that synthesises and evaluates literature in a specific topic area to justify a research questions
Apply appropriate research design and methods to address a specific research question and acknowledge the ethical implications of the research
Develop a research proposal as the basis for a thesis
Present and defend a research proposal

assessments.Question Type: OP1: Each student should make at least 1 individual presentation during the course in front of the class. OP2 (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal
assessments.Note: Participation scores will be given based on students' class attendance, preparation, quantity as well as quality of participation in classroom; quality of participation is demonstrated through asking relevant questions, making statements that add to and facilitate class discussions, and building upon others’ comments. Class participation accounts for 15% of the final score.

assessments.Question Type: OP1: The class should be divided into 4 or 6 groups. Each group will choose a business/management problem to formulate a research topic and corresponding research questions/objectives. The report should include research topic, research rationale, and research questions/objectives. OP2 (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal OP3: Complete the Guided Project -Basic data analysis using SPSS
assessments.No Question: OP1: Maximum length of the assignment should be 2 pages excluding appendices OP2 (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Combination of all relevant acquired knowledge, and research and written skills
assessments.Grading Guide: For presentation, the instructor will make a random order of group presentations. All individuals need to give feedback to other groups' presentation.
assessments.Note: All assignments should be typed and double-spaced with 12-point font, and must be submitted in both soft and hard copy. A deduction of 10% of the assignment mark will be applied for each day of late submission. Assignment score for each student should be based on: (1) Group Assignment Report (50%); (2) individual presentation, Q&A on Group report or individual feedback to other groups' presentations (50%). Group Assignment 1 accounts for 10% of the final score.
